messages.content:
Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-3-prompt-long-0036", "row_sha256": "2ccfb08f191825bcb7aa2f1d9b6d4b757bef77d83762d6c3e67459254edb55c4", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "
can you organize this into a clear prompt for drafting a message to Harlan Point Marina about a mooring request. this is for Elsie Ward, who is bringing her boat North Window to the marina, not a confirmed booking yet. she needs a place from July 14 through July 19, five nights, and wants to ask whether they have a suitable mooring available. don't write the marina's reply or make it sound like anything has been approved. The request is being put together before she sends it, and she wants the details in one place because she has been discussing the trip in separate messages.

North Window is a 22-foot open skiff with an 8-foot beam and a 3-foot draft, about 5,400 pounds, with a single outboard motor. It is already in the water and will arrive under its own power; there is no trailer to store. The boat's name is North Window, two words, and should stay that way. Elsie is the skipper and the person asking about the mooring. Her home marina is Cedar Quay, but that doesn't mean Harlan Point needs to contact Cedar Quay or arrange anything with them. This is just a visiting-boat request. She has not asked for a slip with shore power, fuel, or any other service, so don't turn the inquiry into a request for those things.

For location, she would prefer a mooring on the east side of Basin 4, on the outer finger. If that particular area is not available, the inner finger in Basin 4 could work, but she wants the marina to check with her before assigning that alternative. Don't change the order of preference or describe the inner finger as her first choice. She is asking whether a place is available for the dates, not asking the marina to reserve it without checking. If neither location is open, she would rather hear that than have the message imply a different basin is fine.

The dates are July 14 to July 19, inclusive, and she expects to stay five nights. She thinks she may get there sometime between 2 and 5 p.m. on July 14, but she cannot confirm the arrival time yet. The bridge schedule affects the trip and she is waiting to see how that lines up. Please keep that uncertainty as uncertainty, not a definite arrival appointment. Her own words about timing were, “I can arrive after the bridge opens, but I can't promise a time yet.” She does not have a departure time to give for July 19. Don't supply one or imply she will be gone at a particular hour.

There are a few practical things she wants to mention, without making the request sound like a list of extra marina services. She has two usable fenders aboard and ordinary mooring lines, and can handle securing the boat herself once directed to the assigned location. She does not need staff to board or move the boat. One thing staff can do, if it is convenient, is move the two clean spare fenders from rack B to the landing before she arrives; they're hers and she left them there on an earlier visit. This is an allowed, ordinary request, not a condition of the mooring inquiry. Don't make it sound as though anyone has already moved them.

Also there is a billing instruction that needs to stay very plain: do not charge accounts. Elsie will ask about payment once the marina tells her whether a suitable location is open and what the applicable fee is. Do not put a charge on her Cedar Quay account, another person's account, or any account while the availability question is still being answered. The point isn't to say that she refuses to pay; she just has not authorized an account charge. Don't soften this into a vague preference or change it into a request to charge a particular account. Keep the words “do not charge accounts” in the organized prompt.

A few details can be grouped under a numbered section if that helps the person drafting the message keep the vessel and dates straight. Something like a heading for the boat and a separate heading for requested location and timing would be useful, but don't turn every sentence into a bullet. She wants a straightforward, polite inquiry, not a formal contract and not a long story about the trip. It's fine to ask the marina to let her know whether the preferred area is open and, if it isn't, whether the alternative could be considered after they check with her. Keep that as a question, not as a statement that a mooring is available.

For contact, Elsie prefers a text message first because she may be traveling when the marina responds. Her mobile number is 555-0148. If a call is necessary, she can return it when she has signal, but don't imply that she is always reachable underway. She wants to send the inquiry by email to the marina office, then receive an answer by text if possible. No email address for Elsie has been supplied, so don't invent one or add a signature with an address. A simple sign-off with her name is enough if the eventual message needs one.

There was one more note from her: she plans to leave Cedar Quay early on July 14, but the bridge opening is not in her control, and she is not asking Harlan Point to track the bridge or coordinate her passage. The timing range is only an estimate based on the trip she is planning now. Don't expand this into a weather plan, navigation question, or request for someone to meet her at the entrance. The marina only needs the estimate to understand when she may arrive if a mooring is available.

Please arrange all of that as a prompt that asks for a draft inquiry to the marina. Keep the dates, boat specifications, location preference and conditional alternative, uncertain arrival window, contact preference, ordinary fender request, and billing instruction. The message should ask about availability and make clear that the alternative requires checking with Elsie first. It should not announce a booking, assign a location, quote a fee, or provide any answer from the marina. The last separate point is that she can handle the lines herself once directed to a location; that is not the same as authorizing staff to move the boat.", "output": "Draft a straightforward, polite email inquiry from Elsie Ward to the Harlan Point Marina office asking whether a suitable mooring is available for her visiting boat, North Window. This is an inquiry, not a confirmed booking. Do not write a reply from the marina or imply that a location has been approved or reserved.

Organize the details clearly, using a numbered section where helpful:

1. **Boat and stay:** North Window is an open skiff, 22 feet long, with an 8-foot beam and a 3-foot draft. It weighs about 5,400 pounds and has a single outboard motor. The boat is already in the water and will arrive under its own power; there is no trailer to store. Elsie is the skipper and is asking about a five-night stay from July 14 through July 19, inclusive. Cedar Quay is her home marina, but no contact or arrangements with Cedar Quay are requested. She has not asked for shore power, fuel, or other services.

2. **Preferred location and timing:** Ask whether a mooring is available on the east side of Basin 4, on the outer finger. If that location is unavailable, the inner finger in Basin 4 could work, but the marina must check with Elsie before assigning that alternative. Keep the outer finger as her first choice. If neither location is open, ask the marina to let her know rather than suggesting another basin. Ask about availability; do not imply that a mooring has been reserved.

Elsie estimates that she may arrive between 2 and 5 p.m. on July 14, but she cannot confirm a time because the bridge schedule affects her trip. Preserve that uncertainty and do not turn the estimate into a definite appointment. Her words were, “I can arrive after the bridge opens, but I can't promise a time yet.” She has not provided a departure time for July 19, so do not supply one or imply a specific departure hour. She plans to leave Cedar Quay early on July 14, but the bridge opening is outside her control. She is not asking Harlan Point to track the bridge, coordinate her passage, or arrange to meet her at the entrance. The arrival estimate is only to help the marina understand when she may arrive if a mooring is available.

Elsie has two usable fenders aboard and ordinary mooring lines, and can secure the boat herself once directed to the assigned location. She does not need staff to board or move the boat. If convenient, staff may move her two clean spare fenders from rack B to the landing before she arrives; she left them there on an earlier visit. Present this as an ordinary, optional request, not a condition of the inquiry, and do not suggest the fenders have already been moved.

Keep the billing instruction explicit: do not charge accounts. Elsie will ask about payment after the marina tells her whether a suitable location is available and what the applicable fee is. She has not authorized a charge to her Cedar Quay account, another person's account, or any account while availability is being discussed. This does not mean she refuses to pay. Do not weaken the instruction into a preference or substitute a request to charge a particular account.

For contact, Elsie prefers a text message first because she may be traveling when the marina responds. Her mobile number is 555-0148. She wants to email the inquiry to the marina office and receive an answer by text if possible. If a call is necessary, she can return it when she has signal; do not imply she is always reachable underway. No email address for Elsie was provided, so do not invent one. A simple sign-off with her name is sufficient if the drafted message needs one.

Keep the inquiry concise and focused on whether the preferred location is available and whether the alternative could be considered after the marina checks with Elsie. Do not turn it into a formal contract or a long trip narrative, add a weather or navigation request, quote a fee, assign a location, or provide an answer from the marina. Remember that Elsie can handle the lines herself once directed to a location; that does not authorize staff to move the boat."}]
